 Judgment
This is a claim petition filed by the petitioner claiming compensation of .10,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for the injuries sustained by the petitioner.

2. The petition averments in brief is that on 10.07.2021 at about 7.50 p.m., when he was riding his Dio Scooter bearing Regn.No.KA-05-KV-7439 on the extreme left side of the road Near Mahaveer Lake Apartments, Uttarahalli main road, Bengaluru, at that time the driver of Lorry bearing Regn.No.AP-26-TF-5641 driven by its driver at high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against his vehicle.
Due to which, he fell down and sustained grievous injuries and thereafter Sri.

1
he was shifted to Pathway Hospital, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and spent .1,00,000/- towards his treatment, medicines, conveyances, nourishment and other incidental charges.
Prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy and was Mechanic by profession and earning a sum of .15,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, he became permanent disablement.
The accident occurred only due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by its driver.
The respondent being the owner of offending vehicle is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

3. In spite of service of notice, respondent did not appear before the tribunal hence, he has been placed as ex- parte.
4.

Now the points that arise for my consideration as follows:
POINTS 1. Whether petitioner proves that, he sustained grievous injuries in the accident that occurred on 10.07.2021 at about 7.50 p.m., Near Mahaveer Lake Apartment,
Uttarahalli Main Road, Kengeri, Bengaluru city, while he was proceeding on a Dio Scooter bearing Registration No.KA-05-KV-7439 as a rider, due to the rash and negligent driving of Lorry bearing Registration No.AP-26-TF-5641 by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the claim petition?

If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom?
3.
What order or award?

5. In order to prove case of petitioner, petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and Dr.Banu Prakash A.S. working as Consultant Neurosurgeon and Spine Surgeon at Kshema Specialists Clinic examined as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.16 and closed his side of evidence.
6. I have heard arguments and perused the material available on record.

7. Findings of this tribunal on the above points are as under:-
 Point No.1 : In the Affirmative;
 Point No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative;
 Point No.3 : As per final order for the following:-
 -:REASONS:-
8. Point No.1:- In this case the petitioner contend that on 10-7-2021 at about 07.50 p.m., Near Mahaveer Lake Apartment, Uttarahalli Main Road, Kengeri, Bengaluru city, he had met with an Sri.Krishna.S vs Balaji Ware Housing Corporation Pvt on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40435941/
2 accident due to rash and negligent driving of Lorry bearing Regn.No.AP-26-TF-5641 by its driver and he sustained injuries in the said accident.
9.

sentences.text: The petitioner examined himself as PW.1, in his chief examination he has deposed that due to negligence on the part of driver of lorry, the accident occurred.
In order to prove negligence of driver, the petitioner has produced Ex.P.1 and 2 FIR and first information.
On perusal of Ex.P.2, the mother of petitioner by name Smt.Manjula Sampangi has lodged a first information with police on 10.07.2021.
On the basis of Ex.P.2 police registered a case as per Ex.P.1 for the offence punishable U/s.279, 337 & 338 of IPC.
She has stated in her first information that due to rash and negligent driving of Lorry, the accident occurred.
After registering the case Police went near place of accident and drew up Sketch and Spot Panchanama as per Ex.P.3 & 4 by narrating the place of accident.
On perusal of sketch it shows that due to negligence of driver of offending vehicle the accident occurred.
Ex.P.5 - IMV Report, wherein mentioned that the damages caused to vehicle.
Ex . P.6
Wound certificate shows that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident.
After investigation police filed charge sheet as per Ex.P.7 against driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.279, 337 & 338 of IPC.
The respondent did not appear before the tribunal to disprove the case of petitioner.
The respondent remained absent and placed ex-parte.
The evidence of PW1 remain unchallenged.
So, on perusal of all oral and documentary evidence placed by the petitioner, it clearly show that due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle the accident occurred.
On meticulous perusal of entire case the respondent did not place any material to disprove the case of petitioner.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P.7, this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Lorry bearing Regn.No.AP-26-TF-5641 by its driver and petitioner sustained injuries.
Hence, I answered Point No.1 in the Affirmative.
10. Point No.2:
In view of held Point No.1 in the Affirmative, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

To assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several factors like injury,
pain and suffering sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment and medical attendants, conveyance, loss of income during treatment, disability, loss of amenities etc., let me discussion one by one.
(i) Towards injury and pain and suffering:- The petitioner contended that due to accident he sustained injuries and underwent surgery and later discharged with an advice to take follow up treatment.

In order to prove injuries caused to him,
petitioner has produced wound certificate marked at Ex.P.6 issued by Pathway Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein opinion of the doctor that the injury No.1 is simple in nature and injury No.2, 3 and 4 are grievous in nature.
So, on perusal of records he took treatment in hospital as an inpatient and the petitioner examined Dr.Banu Prakash.A.S. as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P.14 to Ex.P.16.
PW.2/doctor has deposed that he examined the petitioner for assessment of disability and he assessed the disability for permanent physical impairment to the extent of 40%.
By considering the injuries and facts and circumstances of the case, the tribunal is of the view that the compensation of .55,000/- is just and reasonable towards pain and suffering.
Sri. Krishna.

sentences.text: 3 (ii) Towards Medical Expenses:
The petitioner has claimed compensation towards medical expenses.
The petitioner contended that he took treatment at Hospital.
The petitioner has produced 21 medical bills for .1,09,618/- marked at Ex.P.9.
The respondent not rebutted the medical bills by placing cogent evidence.
So, Tribunal is of the view that compensation of .1,09,618/- is just and reasonable towards medical expenses.
(iii) Towards food, extra nourishment and medical attendant charges:
On perusal of records, the accident occurred on 10.07.2021 and the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient in the hospital.
On perusal of evidence, the petitioner was inpatient at Hospital as he has sustained injuries.

So,
during the time of treatment the petitioner also required good food and extra nourishment.

The petitioner has produced Discharge Summary issued by Pathway Hospital marked at Ex.P.8, wherein petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient from 10.07.2021 to 13.07.2021 i.e., for a period of 4 days.

Considering the said facts, the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of .400/- per day for 4 days to a sum of .1,600/- is just and reasonable towards food, extra nourishment and medical attendant.
(iv) Towards Conveyance:

The petitioner is the resident of Channasandra Layout,
Rajarajeshwarinagar, Bengaluru and accident occurred Near Mahaveer Lake Apartment, Uttarahalli Main Road, Kengeri, Bengaluru city, he has admitted for treatment at Hospital.
In order to prove this aspect the petitioner has produced discharge summary.
Considering the injuries and facts of the case, the tribunal is of view that the compensation of .10,000/- is just and proper towards conveyance charges.
(v) Towards loss of income during treatment:
The petitioner has contended that he was doing Mechanic work and earning a sum of .15,000/- per month.
In order to prove his income, the petitioner has not produced any document to show that he was earning .15,000/- per month.
In the absence of positive documents regarding his occupation and income, this tribunal will consider notional income.
Due to the accidental injuries, the petitioner might have not attended his regular work at least for a period of 2 months.
The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka fixed notional income of the year 2021 at .15,000/- per month for determination of income before Lok Adalat.

So, in view of fixing of notional income by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, it is just and proper to this Tribunal to follow the notional income as fixed by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka to decide the cases before this Tribunal also.
Case on hand the petitioner has not produced any relevant document to prove his income.
Accordingly, the notional income of petitioner during the year 2021 treated as .15,000/- per month as fixed by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka.
Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for .30,000/- (15,000/- x 2) towards loss of income during treatment.
(v) Towards Permanent Disability:
The petitioner has contended that due to accident, he was inpatient at hospital, and sustained permanent disablement.

The petitioner also examined Dr.Banu Prakash.A.S. working as Consultant Neurosurgeon at Kshema Specialists clinic,
Bengaluru, examined as PW.2.
PW.2/Doctor examined the patient clinically and radiologically for assessment of disabilities.

The doctor deposed that petitioner has Sri.Krishna.S vs Balaji Ware Housing Corporation Pvt on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40435941/
4 sustained head injury, swelling in the head region, multiple abrasion on right side of the face, loss of consciousness and ENT bleed, GCS 10/15, CT showed left fronto tempero parietal extra axial hematoma with mass effect, subgaleal hematoma is seen in the right supraorbital region, unsuspected fracture of orbital bone with surgical emphysema.

sentences.text: The doctor has examined the petitioner for assessment of disability and assessed the disability to permanent physical impairment at 40%.
In order to prove the disability, doctor has produced Ex.P.14 to 16 documents i.e., OPD slip, Neuro psychological assessment and disability certificate.
By considering the oral and documentary evidence and facts and circumstances of the case, it appears that the petitioner can do his work with difficulty.

Therefore,
considering all these aspects, the functional disability is assessed at 21%.

In order to prove age of the petitioner, he has produced Ex.P.10 - Notarized copy of Aadhaar Card, wherein the date of birth is mentioned as 07.09.1996, the accident occurred on 10.07.2021, so the age of petitioner was 25 years as on the date of accident.
Hence, the same is taken into consideration for applying multiplier and multiplier '18' is applicable as per Smt. Sarla Verma case.
As per ratio laid down by Hon'ble supreme court in Raj Kumar V/s. Ajay kumar and another, this tribunal not deducted personal expenses of petitioner out of his gross income.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Hence, future earning capacity of the petitioner due to permanent disability works out as under :
Annual Income before accident : (15,000/- x 12) = .1,80,000/- Loss of future earning p.a. (21% of prior annual income) .37,800/-.
Multiplier applicable with reference to age - 18 Loss of future earnings - (.37,800/- x 18) = .6,80,400/-.
The petitioner is entitled for .6,80,400/- under the head of loss of future earning capacity.

(vi) Deprivation of Future Amenities:-
The doctor has opined that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries and he is unable to do his day-today activities as earlier.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the tribunal is of the view that compensation of .10,000/- is just and reasonable under the head deprivation of future amenities.

11. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:

12.

In MFA.No.100090 of 2014 C/w. MFA.No.25107 of 2013 between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs. Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another, the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka at Page No.7 at Para No.15 held as follows:
"However, the provisions of Section 149(1) of the Act to the extent they speak of interest payable on the compensation amount is in the nature of an exception to the general law enacted in 169 of the M.V.Act and therefore, the provisions of Section 34 of CPC to that extent become invocable on the general principles of construction of statutes namely the special law overrides the general law.

entities.text: Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs. Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, in the absence of any other law relating to interest on Judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Section 34 of CPC, 1908.

Thus, in the given circumstances of this case,
interest at the rate of more than 6% could not have been awarded."

In view of ratio and dictum laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the above judgment, the petitioners are entitled for interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
13. The petitioner has filed petition against the respondent.
It is already held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Lorry bearing Regn.No.AP-26- TF-5641 by its driver.
So, the respondent being the owner of the offending vehicle is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, Issue No.2 answered Partly in the Affirmative.
14. Issue No.3:

In view of the findings given on the above said issues, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioner Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation amount of .8,96,618/- (Rupees Eight Lakhs Ninety Six Thousand Six Hundred and Eighteen only) with interest at 6% p.a.,
from the date of petition till realization.
Respondent being RC owner of offending vehicle is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner and to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.

In the event of deposit of the said compensation amount, 40% shall be deposited in the name of petitioner for a period of 3 years in any nationalized bank or scheduled Sri.Krishna.S vs Balaji Ware Housing Corporation Pvt on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40435941/
6 bank and the remaining 60% shall be released in favour of petitioner on proper identification.
